ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure below, $\angle A=70^\circ$, BP and CP bisect $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ACB$ respectively. What is the measure of $\angle P$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A = 70^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC + \angle ACB = 180^\circ - \angle A = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$,\\
$\because BP$ and $CP$ bisect $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ACB$ respectively,\\
$\therefore \angle PBC = \frac{1}{2} \angle ABC$, $\angle PCB = \frac{1}{2} \angle ACB$,\\
In $\triangle PBC$,\\
$\angle P + \angle PBC + \angle PCB = 180^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle P = 180^\circ - (\angle PBC + \angle PCB) = 180^\circ - \frac{1}{2} (\angle ABC + \angle ACB) = 180^\circ - \frac{1}{2} \times 110^\circ = \boxed{125^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; point P is located inside triangle ABC, line segments BP and CP have been drawn, therefore forming the internal triangle PBC. The problem text states ∠A = 70°, and BP and CP respectively bisect ∠ABC and ∠ACB. Then reason: Let ∠ABC = B, ∠ACB = C. Because the sum of the interior angles of triangle ABC is 180°, so B + C = 180° - 70° = 110°. Since BP bisects ∠ABC, ∠PBC = B/2; since CP bisects ∠ACB, ∠PCB = C/2. In triangle PBC, ∠P + ∠PBC + ∠PCB = 180°, therefore ∠P = 180° - (B/2 + C/2) = 180° - (B + C)/2 = 180° - 110°/2 = 180° - 55° = 125°.
